title: International Studies
sourceText:
Academic Programs and Pathways

Degrees and Certificates

International Studies

International Studies

In the age of globalization, it is more important than ever to understand geopolitical identities, positions, and business practices. International Studies offers students key insights into the current realities of world affairs and relations between global entities. International Studies offers a course map to get you major ready to transfer.

Visit Program Website

Program Information

                Program Type
                Associate Degree - Transfer

                Degree
                Associate in Arts and Sciences - Direct Transfer Agreement

                                  Duration
                  90 credits

                                  Program Prerequisite

None

                Pathway

Social Science, Public Service & Community Engagement

                                  Focus Areas

International Studies

Course Maps

A course map is a quick guide to help students figure out which courses to take each quarter. Course maps were written by BC faculty, who have used their expertise to recommend specific courses students can take to achieve their academic or career goals. Students should meet with an advisor to learn more.

International Studies, AAS-DTA

Sample Courses

Geography of World Affairs

International Business

Global History

Middle East Politics and Society

Cultural Interactions in an Interdependent World

          Featured Faculty

Ian Walker

Program Chair

Ian Walker received his Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Washington State University and a Master of Arts in Human Geography from Swansea University in Wales. He has taught several physical geography courses including Weather and Climate, the Violent Face of Nature, and Cartography and Landforms.

Leslie Lum

Faculty

Leslie Lum has an MBA from Columbia University and a MSW in social work from the University of British Columbia. She has extensive industry experience including strategic planning at a Fortune 100 and investment banking with a global bank. She was selected for the 2016 Lockwood Award for Faculty Excellence and Innovation.

Salam Awad

Faculty

Salam Awad received her Bachelor’s degree in Political Science from Central Washington University and her M.A. in Political Science from University of Illinois Springfield. Her research and teaching interests include international relations, post colonial studies, the Middle East, social movements, refugees and human rights.
